reviews.review:
We visited MotiMahal Restaurant in the Gerrard India Bazaar and enjoyed experiencing one of Toronto’s longest-running Indian restaurants. Serving the community since 1976, Moti Mahal has been a neighborhood landmark for generations and offers a casual, welcoming atmosphere, offering a mix of Indian street food, curries, thalis, sweets, and traditional favorites.

The restaurant has a long history and connection to Toronto’s Little India community. And, the menu offers a wide variety of options, from quick snacks and street food to full meals and freshly made sweets prepared in-house.

We were impressed with their selection of Indian sweets. The display offered a great variety of traditional desserts, and we ended up getting a mixed box to take home.

The restaurant itself isn’t super clean or fancy, but the food more than makes up for it. If you’re looking for real, old-school North Indian comfort food, Moti Mahal is a must-visit.

reviews.review:
I’ve been a regular at Moti Mahal Restaurant for over six years now. This place is run by a wonderful elderly couple who are incredibly warm and kind—even today, they still head into the kitchen every single day to personally cook and oversee the dishes. The staff here is always professional and welcoming, making you feel right at home the moment you walk in.
?You can always find the perfect lunch to satisfy your cravings here. From their crispy samosas and traditional naan to my personal favorite—the lamb biryani—plus a great selection of desserts, they have it all. If you’re looking to experience authentic, time-honored Indian flavors, I highly recommend checking this place out!

It was fairly busy when we were there with lots of groups of family and friends there. You can't go wrong with this place.
Food: 5/5  |  Service: 5/5  |  Atmosphere: 4/5

Recommended dishes
Channa Bhatura, Raj Kachori, Chicken Tikka, Kulfi

reviews.review: This place needs to improve seriously. I remember visiting it in 2019 when their hygiene was a little better but now they might as well be making people sick. I got their chole bhature and started vomiting as soon as I got back home. I had severe stomachache for the next few days. Their kitchen has stale food and nobody in the staff has any hygiene manners. It’s never properly mopped and you can even smell an eerie stinky smell. Please please please take proper measures as people’s health is affected when you don’t. In the pictures, you can look at the amount of oil used in there. I didn’t even finish half of it and still got sick. Never going back unless they fix their hygiene.

reviews.review: Moti Mahal has existed in this neighbourhood for many years. It offers a mixture of Delhi style street food with South Indian dosas. There are many restaurants in Gerrard Street that offer a diverse mixture of South Asian dishes, but if I'm here in this neighbourhood, I would prefer Moti Mahal.

reviews.review:
I recently visited Moti Mahal for some Indian street food cravings and had a mixed experience. We ordered a variety of chaat items including sweets. The Raj Kachori was a bit disappointing it resembled more of a basket chaat and lacked the authentic flavor and presentation I expected. However, we also did a takeout of Chole Bhature, and it was delicious. A definite must-try if you visit!

Overall, a decent spot for Indian snacks, but stick to the classics like Chole Bhature for the best experience.
Food: 3/5  |  Service: 5/5  |  Atmosphere: 4/5

reviews.review:
Decent food. I ordered chana bhatura, tandoori chicken and fish pakora. None of the dishes stood out, to be honest. It was just average South Asian food. The chana itself was very salty and the tandoori chicken was well seasoned but not especially moist. The fish pakora isn't worth it at all — small fish pieces in a lot of batter. I don't think I'll be getting food from Moti mahal again.

reviews.review:
We tried following items,
- Mango Lassi - 1.5/5 - Was bitter for some reason
- Falooda - 1/5 - was watered down
- Channa Bhature - 3.5/5 - this was great but channa and bhature was a bit oily.
- Pani Puri - 5/5 - it was the best thing we got.

We took take-out and here are some other stuff we noticed,

Staff - 5/5 - super friendly, we didn’t have to wait too long for food to get ready even though there were a lot of people dining in at the time.
Hygiene - 2/5 - we found dirt on the outside container for the drinks which was off-putting. Also staff was using windex to clean tables as opposed to actual sanitary solutions.

Giving 3/5 for the overall experience here.
Food: 5/5  |  Service: 5/5  |  Atmosphere: 4/5

Indoor dining area, Counter seating

reviews.review: The place is pretty narrow, and with chairs in the middle, we didn't feel so comfortable walking to the counter to make an order. Service was pretty fast, and it didn't take long for our order to be ready. Portions are decent size for the price, we ate half of what we ordered and took other half home. Everything tasted good, naan bread was a little to oily, but still very delicious. In our opinion reusable plastic plates could be replaced with proper ones and disposable cutlery could also be replaced with more sustainable options. Overall good experience and worth to visit at least once.
reviews.author: Nishit Shah
